viv: FYI ran a medium-scale comparison for the new reranker-v2 (PTQ int8) to understand the priming tradeoffs. I built an "effect matrix" that slices by corpus / query_len / html_noise and includes bootstrap CI + tie-rate columns. Getting mixed signals: KB-style corpora benefit, transactional/support corpora show MRR regressions.

samir: Nice. Did you compute statistical significance (bootstrap p-values) per slice?

viv: Yes 1000 bootstrap samples per slice. Columns in the effect matrix: corpus, slice_key, n, ndcg_base, ndcg_primed, ndcg_delta, ndcg_pval, mrr_base, mrr_primed, mrr_delta, mrr_pval, tie_rate_base, tie_rate_primed, tie_rate_delta, score_gap_std_base, score_gap_std_primed. I uploaded CSV to s3: s3://bench/artifacts/7390012345/effect_matrix.csv

zoe: Can you paste a small excerpt and the global aggregates?

viv: excerpt (top rows):

```
corpus,slice_key,n,ndcg_base,ndcg_primed,ndcg_delta,ndcg_pval,mrr_base,mrr_primed,mrr_delta,mrr_pval,tie_rate_base,tie_rate_primed,tie_rate_delta,score_gap_std_base,score_gap_std_primed
kb,long-ambiguous,1200,0.713,0.729,0.016,0.001,0.462,0.456,-0.006,0.12,0.043,0.049,0.006,0.0028,0.0036
support,short-html,900,0.658,0.643,-0.015,0.02,0.402,0.381,-0.021,0.005,0.051,0.092,0.041,0.0031,0.0067
faq,medium,700,0.724,0.732,0.008,0.04,0.488,0.485,-0.003,0.26,0.037,0.041,0.004,0.0026,0.0030
```

viv: Global aggregate (n=50000): ndcg_delta +0.004 (p=0.03), mrr_delta -0.006 (p=0.01). Tie-rate increased on short-html slices.

samir: So priming reduces score gaps and increases tie flips in html-heavy short queries. Did you look at tokenization diffs and a mitigation matrix?

viv: Yes. I computed token_shift_index = mean position of first changed subword. For short-html slice token_shift_index=0.4 (most changes at first token). Mitigations we tried: (A) strip-html upstream, (B) punctuation-safe sentinel "Query:\n", (C) unicode non-joiner U+200C between sentinel and query, (D) disable priming for specific corpus route, (E) PTQ recalibration w/ multiple seeds.

zoe: Which mitigations reduced MRR regression most?

viv: Quick ranking by MRR recovery on support short-html slice: strip-html (~95% recovery), non-joiner (~80%), punct-safe sentinel (~60%), PTQ re-calib seeds variability (~40% avg improvement but inconsistent). Disabling priming for support obviously removes regression but loses KB gains.

samir: Did you try measurement-only deterministic tie-breaker to quantify tie flips' contribution?

viv: Yes. I added a flag ranker.eval.tie_policy=deterministic_docid so we could count how many placements change only due to tie flips (without changing scores). That reduced the net MRR delta by ~30% on short-html slice, implying tie flips are a sizable contributor but not all of it.

zoe: Good. What about quant noise? How much did PTQ seeds affect results?

viv: Ran PTQ calibration with seeds [1,7,42,99]. Per-slice score_gap_std varied; short-html had post-quant score_gap_std mean 0.0067 vs base 0.0031. Seed variance produced +-0.002 MRR delta swing in worst slices. So PTQ amplifies the effect but isn't the root cause.

samir: Can you paste the eval command templates you used so we can reproduce?

viv: baseline command for the primed arm:

```
./eval/eval_rerank \
  --model models/ranker-v2-int8.ptq \
  --holdout s3://bench/holdouts/2026-06-01.json \
  --priming templates/primed_v2.json \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --samples 50000 \
  --emit-token-diff --emit-deltas --bootstrap 1000 \
  --tie_policy=none --out s3://bench/artifacts/7390012345/primed_run.json
```

and for non-joiner sentinel trial:

```
./eval/eval_rerank \
  --model models/ranker-v2-int8.ptq \
  --holdout s3://bench/holdouts/2026-06-01.json \
  --priming templates/nonjoiner-sentinel.json \
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --samples 50000 \
  --emit-token-diff --emit-deltas --bootstrap 1000 \
  --tie_policy=deterministic_docid --out s3://bench/artifacts/7390012345/nonjoiner_run.json
```

viv: All artifacts and the effect_matrix.csv uploaded to s3://bench/artifacts/7390012345/. eval-bot queued remaining mitigation runs.

eval-bot: job 7390012350 started: eval_rerank (arms=primed,nonjoiner,punctsafe,raw; samples=50k; bootstrap=1000).

zoe: Next steps / recommendation?

samir: From the effect matrix risk profile: KB gains are robust and significant for long-ambiguous queries. Support regressions are concentrated in html-heavy short queries and are explainable by token-merge + PTQ amplification. I recommend a two-step rollout: (1) enable priming by default for KB-like routes (corpus routing) with monitoring, (2) for support routes either disable priming or enable priming only after upstream stripping of formatting, (3) push a non-joiner sentinel as a lower-risk global mitigation while we measure long-term PTQ stability, (4) add per-route canary gates that monitor slice-level MRR with bootstrap pvals and auto-rollback if p<0.01 and delta exceeds threshold.

zoe: Agree. Please add a short scorecard (1-pager) for the PLG/Docs team summarizing risk and recommended routing rules. Also include the effect_matrix CSV and a short README describing slice keys and bootstrap methodology.

viv: Will do. I'll open an RFC with the recommendation and attach artifacts + the effect matrix + scripts to reproduce. Tagging @eng-platform for routing work. :white_check_mark:
